name: Sivaloka Thyagesar Temple, Tirunallur Perumanam
deity: Shiva as Sivalokathyagesar (Sivaloka Thyagar), with the goddess Venneetru Umaiammai (Swetha Vibhuti Nayaki)
period: Ancient Shaiva shrine sung in the Tevaram by Sambandar (7th century); believed to be a Pallava foundation, renovated in the Chola period
summary: Sivalokathyagesar of Tirunallur Perumanam, today's Achalpuram, is the temple where the child-saint Sambandar was wed and then entered the light of Shiva with his bride and all the wedding guests, the great wedding that gave the Tevaram town its name.

sections.history: Tirunallur Perumanam, the village of Nallur and its great wedding, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam praised in the Tevaram by the child-saint Sambandar. The place is known today as Achalpuram, in the Sirkazhi taluk of Mayiladuthurai district, a short drive from Sirkazhi, where the saint was born, and from Chidambaram. Tradition believes the temple to have been founded under the Pallavas and fully renovated by the medieval Cholas, and the goddess's shrine is dated to the year 1210. The name Perumanam, the great wedding, records the event for which the town is remembered, and which the Periya Puranam tells in the life of Sambandar.
sections.architecture: The temple faces east and is entered beneath a five-tiered rajagopuram. Beyond it stand the metal-clad flagstaff and the Nandi mandapam, and beyond these a hundred-pillared hall that houses a shrine to Sambandar shown with his bride. The sanctum holds the Shiva linga of Sivalokathyagesar, and the goddess Venneetru Umaiammai, also called Swetha Vibhuti Nayaki, the mother of the white ash, is honoured in her own shrine. The temple has eleven sacred tanks, of which the Panchakshara Theertham, opposite the eastern entrance, is the chief, and the mango is the sacred tree of the place.
sections.legends: The legend of Tirunallur Perumanam is the wedding of Sambandar. His father, Sivapada Hridayar, wished to see his son married and chose Mangai Nallal, also called Stotrapoornambikai, the daughter of Nambandar Nambi of the neighbouring village of Nallur. The wedding was arranged at the temple, with the Nayanar Tiruneelanakka presiding over the rites and guests, among them Muruga Nayanar, gathering from near and far. Sambandar is said to have prayed to the Lord to keep him from the entanglements of household life. As the rites went forward a brilliant beam of divine light appeared, and the Lord bade the saint come to him with all who were assembled. Sambandar sang the Namashivaya hymn to reassure those who hesitated, and then he, his bride, his parents and the whole wedding company entered the light and merged with the Lord. The great wedding became a wedding with Shiva himself.
sections.festivals: The festival of the place is the remembrance of the wedding, kept each year on the day of the Moolam star in the Tamil month of Vaikasi (May–June), when Sambandar's wedding and his entry into the light are recalled with great devotion. Maha Shivaratri and the monthly Pradosham are observed as at every Shiva temple. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil calendar.
sections.experience: Come to Achalpuram for its one great story, and let it be told slowly. After the gopuram, the flagstaff and the Nandi, walk into the hundred-pillared hall and look at the shrine of Sambandar with his bride before going on to the sanctum of Sivalokathyagesar and the shrine of the goddess. Many visitors pause at the Panchakshara Theertham facing the eastern gate and recite the Namashivaya hymn the saint is said to have sung here. It is a village temple, quiet outside festival days, and families who come for weddings and for blessings on a new marriage hold it especially dear.

visit.timings: Commonly reported as open in the morning until noon and again from about 4 pm to 8 pm; hours vary on festival days, so confirm locally.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected, with shoulders and knees covered: dhoti or trousers for men; saree, salwar kameez or a long skirt for women. Footwear is removed before entering the temple.
visit.photography: Photography is usually allowed in the outer courtyards but not within the sanctum. Please ask the temple staff before photographing priests, rituals or wedding parties.
visit.gettingThere: Achalpuram lies in Sirkazhi taluk, Mayiladuthurai district, roughly 12 km southeast of Chidambaram and 13 km northeast of Sirkazhi, which has the nearest railway station. Buses on the Sirkazhi–Mahendrapuram route pass through the village, and Mayiladuthurai is about 37 km away. Chennai is the principal airport, over 200 km away by road.
